+      - name: Build the documentation site
+        id: docs
+        continue-on-error: true
+        shell: bash
+        env:
+          REPO_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}
+          DOCS_COMMENT_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/px1-docs-impact.md
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          # Until the base commit has the docs command there is nothing to run.
+          if ! grep -q 'os.Args\[1\] == "docs"' main.go; then

+          merge_base="$(git merge-base "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA")"
+          go build -o "${RUNNER_TEMP}/px1-docs-tool" .
+          tool="${RUNNER_TEMP}/px1-docs-tool"

+          "$tool" docs site --root . --out "${build}/docs" \

+          "$tool" docs site --root "$head_tree" --out "${build}/preview" --impact "$impact" \
+            --source-url "${REPO_URL}/blob/${HEAD_SHA}" --commit "${HEAD_SHA:0:7}"
+          # Move into the site only when everything was built.
+          mkdir -p site/docs-preview
+          mv "${build}/docs" site/docs
+          mv "${build}/preview" "site/docs-preview/${HEAD_SHA}"
+          echo "built=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

+## In CI
+
+The review-report workflow builds the documentation with the trusted base
+checkout, after the report history is validated:
+
+- the site for the base commit is published at `docs/` on Pages;
+- a preview for the pull request, with the affected pages marked, is
+  published at `docs-preview/<head sha>/`;
+- the impact report is posted as one pull-request comment that is updated on
+  every push, with a link to the preview.
+
+The pull request's files are checked out as data. `px1 docs` reads Markdown
+and parses source; it builds and runs nothing from them, and it refuses any
+symbolic link that leaves the repository, so a pull request cannot get a file
+from the runner published. The step cannot fail the workflow.
+
+Limits: Pages holds one deployment, so a preview is replaced when another
+pull request is published. Previews run for pull requests from forks too,
+since nothing from them is executed and no secret is involved.

explanations.title: Publish documentation and pull-request previews
explanations.summary: The workflow now builds the base documentation site and a pull-request preview, marking pages affected by the change. It uses the trusted checkout to build the tool and reads the pull-request checkout as data. If the docs build fails, it does not stop the review report from being published.

explanations.title: Keep the impact report comment updated
explanations.summary: After a successful docs build, the workflow creates or updates a single bot comment with the impact report and preview link. Commenting is best-effort, so a comment failure does not fail the workflow.

explanations.title: Refuse links outside the repository
explanations.summary: Documentation reads now resolve symbolic links and reject paths that lead outside the repository. This prevents a pull-request file from pointing at runner data and having that data included in a published site or documentation reference.
